description: Capability-tier routing policy. Data only: changing a model name or a tier mapping must never require editing AGENTS.md or any harness code. Subscription authentication is not subscription usage: an account is dispatchable only through an execution mechanism that consumes its plan's included usage. A logical account slot is not an auth context either: a slot executed through a directory-isolated runtime declares the concrete accountDir its credential lives in, and the mechanism declares the provider id that credential is filed under. `provider` is the vendor axis (tier lookup, cross-provider review independence); `authProvider` is what the runtime is invoked and probed with. They are not interchangeable. A dispatchable mechanism also declares the argv `launch` templates it is started with, per role; a mechanism with no launch declaration cannot be launched by the dispatcher rather than being started by guessed syntax.

CLAUDE_B.conceptualRole: independent Claude reviewer or second hard task

claude-code-cli.basis: Claude Code signed in with a Claude Pro account draws that plan's included usage; observed locally as claude_pro / stripe_subscription (docs/reviews/2026-08-20-pi-harness-implementation.md, section C).

launch.basis: claude --help (2.x): --print is the non-interactive path, --permission-mode acceptEdits lets an executor write inside its own worktree, --add-dir grants the handoff directory it writes its report into (deliberately not under .git, which this runtime treats as sensitive regardless of the grant), and --permission-mode plan is the hard read-only mode a Verifier-Lite reviewer runs under. A reviewer writes nothing at all, so its verdict is read from stdout rather than from a file. --safe-mode is reviewer-only: a reviewer works in a detached checkout of the executor's own commit, so CLAUDE.md, project skills and .claude/settings.json hooks discovered from that directory are files the executor wrote, and auto-loading them lets a candidate configure the process judging it. Verified against CLI 2.1.238 in a scratch checkout: without it the candidate's CLAUDE.md and project skill were both in context and a SessionStart hook executed; with it none of the three did, while the explicit brief was still received. --bare disables the same discovery but forces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper auth (observed: 'Not logged in' with the subscription credential present), which no mechanism here may use. An executor keeps its project instructions; only the reviewer refuses them.

pi-anthropic-oauth.basis: Pi provider documentation: Claude Pro/Max credentials used through Pi are billed per token as Anthropic extra usage rather than against plan limits. Subscription authentication, metered execution — not dispatchable here.

pi-openai-chatgpt-oauth.basis: Pi provider documentation: the OpenAI provider signs in with the Codex ChatGPT Plus/Pro OAuth path, which consumes that plan's included Codex usage. That credential is filed under provider id openai-codex, not openai; probing plain openai reports credentials_not_configured for an account that is in fact ready (observed 2026-08-20 against ~/.pi/accounts/gpt_a).

launch.basis: pi --help (0.84): --print is non-interactive, --thinking carries the effort ladder, --session-dir isolates the session per run, and --tools read is the hard read-only allowlist a reviewer runs under. The provider flag takes the mechanism authProvider, never an account provider. A reviewer writes nothing, so its verdict is read from stdout. --no-context-files and --no-skills are reviewer-only, for the same reason --safe-mode is on the Claude side: a reviewer works in a detached checkout of the executor's own commit, so AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and any skill discovered from that directory are files the executor wrote. Verified against pi 0.84.2 in a scratch checkout: without them the candidate's AGENTS.md was in context; with them it was not, while the explicit brief was still received. An executor keeps its project instructions; only the reviewer refuses them.

arena.standing: routing prior, not an oracle; never overrides a deterministic gate or a reproduction
